items.title: Add 'onParentDelete' alias for 'deleteRule' in ManyToOne options for better readability
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Yes, it is related to code ambiguity and Developer Experience (DX).
Currently, the @ManyToOne decorator uses deleteRule and updateRule properties to configure ON DELETE and ON UPDATE behaviors in the database. However, writing these inside a child entity creates confusion. It is not immediately clear whether the "rule" applies to the deletion/update of the child entity itself or the referenced parent entity. Developers often have to double-check the documentation to remember how the ORM interprets this.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to propose adding more intuitive aliases (or changing them in future major versions) for these properties that clearly state what triggers the action.

Specifically:
- `deleteRule` → `onParentDelete` (or `onReferencedDelete`)
- `updateRule` → `onParentUpdate` (or `onReferencedUpdate`)

Example of how readable the code becomes:
```TS
@ManyToOne(() => User, { onParentDelete: 'cascade', onParentUpdate: 'cascade' })
user: User;
```
Reading this from top to bottom leaves zero ambiguity: "When the parent is deleted/updated, cascade the action."


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keeping deleteRule / updateRule as they are, but it forces developers to think in raw SQL constraints rather than intuitive object-oriented TypeScript definitions while reading the entity code.


**Additional context**
To avoid breaking changes for existing projects, these new names can be introduced as optional aliases in the current major version, with the possibility of deprecating the old *Rule syntax in future major releases.

Key every user-class lookup by class reference, not class name (follow-up to #8107)
items.body:
Follow-up to #8107.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

#8107 asked for the decorator metadata registry to be keyed by class reference "end to end". The fix that landed covers discovery, and it works: `MetadataStorage.getMetadata` keys by `META_SYMBOL`, `initRelation` resolves through `prop.target` before falling back to a name, and a 166-entity schema discovers cleanly under a bundler that mangles every class name.

The assumption that a class name identifies a class survives everywhere around discovery, and those paths are the ones that fail now. Each one costs a production debugging session to find, and several of the remaining ones fail silently rather than throwing.

How bad the collisions are, in a Next.js 16 Turbopack server build: in one chunk, 129 entity classes occupy 17 distinct minified names. One name, `d`, is shared by 19 entities. All six user-defined `Type` subclasses minify to `a`. Collisions are the default under this bundler, not an edge case.

One relevant detail: MikroORM resolves as an external and ships unminified, so its own classes keep their names. Only **user-supplied** classes get mangled. That scopes the problem — every lookup that keys a user class by name is affected, and nothing internal to the library is.

The confirmed failure is in `EventManager`, which dispatches entity events by name:

```js
// events/EventManager.js:87
return new Set(
  listener.getSubscribedEntities().map((name) => Utils.className(name)),
);

// events/EventManager.js:46
if (entities.size === 0 || !entity || entities.has(entity.constructor.name)) {
  listeners.push(listener[event].bind(listener));
}
```

A subscriber declaring `getSubscribedEntities() { return [Foo] }` received `beforeCreate` for an unrelated entity that mangled to the same name, and crashed reading a relation that entity does not have:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')
     at Object.beforeCreate
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**

An audit of every lookup that resolves a user-supplied class, keying each by class reference or `_id` the way discovery now does, rather than another point fix.

Line numbers are from 7.1.14-dev.10. Only the first row is confirmed by a stack trace; the rest come from reading the source, and I have not built a reproduction for each.

| Location                                                                 | Key                                 | Consequence of a collision                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `events/EventManager.js:46,87`                                           | `entity.constructor.name`           | Subscriber runs for a foreign entity. **Confirmed.**                                                                                                                                                             |
| `EntityManager.js:263` (`addFilter`)                                     | `Utils.className(entity)`           | A global filter registered for one entity applies to another. Silent, and a tenancy filter landing on the wrong entity is a data-exposure bug.                                                                   |
| `EntityManager.js:2119` (cache key)                                      | `Utils.className(entityName)`       | Result cache returns another entity's rows for the same method and query shape. Silent.                                                                                                                          |
| `types/Type.js:57` (`Type.getType`)                                      | `cls.name`                          | Returns a cached instance of a different `Type` subclass. Silent value corruption. Discovery uses `new prop.type()` so it is off that path today, but `getType` is public API.                                   |
| `metadata/MetadataStorage.js:91,102`                                     | `Utils.className`                   | `find()` falls back to the class-name map and `set()` writes it, so the last class registered under a shared name wins every name-based lookup.                                                                  |
| `entity/EntityRepository.js:225`                                         | both sides by name                  | `validateRepositoryType` compares two mangled names, so a wrong-entity call passes validation.                                                                                                                   |
| `metadata/MetadataDiscovery.js:2141`                                     | `Utils.className(cls)`              | `forceEntityConstructor: [A, B]` matches unrelated entities.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `metadata/MetadataDiscovery.js:234`, `metadata/MetadataValidator.js:116` | `prop.type` string vs `m.className` | The "entity not discovered" checks pass on a name match against the wrong entity. `MetadataDiscovery.js:228` already pairs its name check with `discoveredByIdentity`; these two did not get the same treatment. |

Where a name is genuinely load-bearing — STI, `discriminatorMap`, `EntitySchema` string names, `em.find('Foo', …)` — keeping it is fine, documented as requiring stable class names. The distinction I would suggest: a class name is fine for producing a message, and never fine for deciding which class something is.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Dropping `getSubscribedEntities()` and narrowing with `instanceof` inside every hook. This works, but it means the documented filtering API cannot be used at all on a minifying bundler.
- Bundler-side `keep_classnames`, requested in vercel/next.js#96574. Next implemented turbopack client only minification configuration in upcoming 16.4 (vercel/next.js#96578)
- `EntitySchema` with explicit names, as #8107 noted, means abandoning the decorator API across the app.

**Additional context**

`@mikro-orm/core` 7.1.14-dev.10, `@mikro-orm/decorators` legacy decorators, `@mikro-orm/postgresql`, Next.js 16.3.3, Turbopack server build with minification on. Explicit `tableName` on all 166 entities, explicit entity arrays, explicit `type` on every property.

Four of these surfaced in a single migration to a minifying bundler: table-name derivation, `discriminatorMap` resolution, the metadata registry from #8107, and the event manager, with #8107's fix already in place for the last one. Happy to test a canary, and I can share the script that produces the collision census above if a reproduction fixture would help.

items.title: Key decorator metadata registry by class reference (_id), not class name — minified builds with mangled class names corrupt discovery
items.body:
# Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Production bundlers that mangle class names still corrupt MikroORM v7's decorator metadata registry. This has become acute with Next.js 16, where Turbopack is the default production bundler, its minifier mangles server-side class names, and there is currently no `keep_classnames` escape hatch (tracked upstream in vercel/next.js#96574, where the Turbopack team's position is that depending on constructor names is a library-level issue).

Minimal reproduction (self-contained, in-memory SQLite, four decorator entities): https://github.com/andres-dejesus/turbopack-mikroorm-mangling-repro

With default Turbopack minification, discovery fails during build-time prerendering:

```
Error [MetadataError]: Duplicate table names are not allowed: reactions
```

In our 24-entity production app the same root cause surfaces at decorator-registration time instead:

```
Error [MetadataError]: Multiple property decorators used on 'd.user' property
```

(the entity class minified to `d`, colliding with another class also minified to `d`).

This is with every known mitigation already applied: explicit `type` on every property (per discussion #6868 — no reliance on `emitDecoratorMetadata` reflection), explicit `tableName` on every entity, and explicit entity arrays (no folder-based discovery).

# Describe the solution you'd like

v7 already went partway here: `MetadataStorage` carries a per-class `_id` and an id-keyed map, and relations resolve through class references. But the registry still maintains `className`-keyed maps alongside, and the decorator registration path collides when two mangled classes share a short name.

The ask: key the decorator metadata registry off the existing `_id`/class-reference machinery end to end, so that mangled class names degrade only error-message readability, never correctness. (STI and other genuinely name-dependent features could keep requiring stable names, documented as such.)

# Describe alternatives you've considered

- `EntitySchema` with explicit `name` — works, but means abandoning the decorator API across the app.
- Bundler-side `keep_classnames` — requested on the Next.js side in vercel/next.js#96574; a team member has signaled openness, but a library-side fix would make MikroORM robust on every bundler with no config, and the two fixes are complementary.
- Disabling server minification — works today on webpack (`experimental.serverMinification: false`), silently ignored by Turbopack; the only Turbopack workaround is disabling minification globally, including client bundles.

# Additional context

MikroORM 7.1.9, `@mikro-orm/decorators` legacy decorators, Next.js 16.3.0. The reproduction repo includes the full pass/fail matrix (Turbopack minified fails; Turbopack unminified and webpack with `serverMinification: false` both pass). Happy to test any canary against it and against our production app.

items.title: Routine.is() uses bare instanceof — breaks under the CJS/ESM dual-package hazard that #7289 fixed for EntitySchema
PostgreSQL dollar-quoted trigger bodies are split at internal semicolons
items.body:
## Describe the bug

PostgreSQL trigger functions generated from entity metadata are dollar-quoted
PL/pgSQL blocks. When the trigger body contains more than one statement,
internal semicolons followed by newlines are treated as migration/schema
statement boundaries.

This affects two public paths:

1. `migrator.createInitial()` returns a split `diff.up`, so the generated
   migration contains separate `addSql()` calls for fragments of one function.
2. `orm.schema.refresh()` executes the same fragments separately and fails with
   `syntax error at or near ";"`.

The generated schema SQL before statement splitting is valid. The split result
from the reproduction is:

```text
create table "items" ("id" serial primary key, "value" int not null default 0);
create or replace function "items_items_increment_after_insert_fn"() returns trigger as $$ begin update items set value = value + 1 where id = NEW.id;
return NEW;; end; $$ language plpgsql;
create trigger "items_increment_after_insert" AFTER INSERT on "items" for each ROW execute function "items_items_increment_after_insert_fn"();
```

But `createInitial().diff.up` contains the function as two entries:

```json
[
  "create or replace function ... where id = NEW.id;",
  "return NEW;; end; $$ language plpgsql;"
]
```

The likely common boundary is the SQL statement splitting that recognizes
single-quoted strings but not PostgreSQL dollar-quoted blocks.

Expected: semicolons/newlines inside `$tag$ ... $tag$` remain part of one SQL
statement for both migration generation and schema execution.

## Reproduction

https://gist.github.com/vkartaviy/bd393135dc77bd8f34fa6cd718e185ac

The gist uses only public `EntitySchema`, `Migrator`, and schema-generator APIs,
pins all MikroORM packages to `7.1.8`, uses pnpm, and includes a PostgreSQL 17
Docker command. `pnpm repro` prints the split migration diff and then reproduces
the `schema.refresh()` syntax error.

## Environment

- Driver: `@mikro-orm/postgresql`
- MikroORM: `7.1.8` (current latest stable)
- Node.js: `v24.14.1`
- pnpm: `11.0.0` in the standalone reproduction
- PostgreSQL: `17`
- OS: macOS `26.5.2`

## Validations

- Read the contributing guidelines and docs.
- Searched open and closed issues for trigger-body, dollar-quoted, PL/pgSQL,
  migration-splitting, and schema-refresh reports.
- Reproduced from a clean standalone pnpm install and dedicated PostgreSQL
  database.

items.title: migration:up poisons snapshot with migration-owned external triggers
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`migrator.up()` rewrites the migration snapshot from live introspection. If a
migration creates a PostgreSQL trigger with custom SQL, that trigger is copied
into the entity-metadata snapshot even though it is not declared in entity
metadata.

The next `migrator.checkSchema()` returns `true` and `migration:check` asks for a
new migration that drops the trigger. This makes migration-owned PostgreSQL
artifacts and snapshots incompatible.

### Reproduction

Minimal pnpm-only reproduction:

https://gist.github.com/vkartaviy/3607e3da5111d8f659a50f84df6394f0

It uses one `EntitySchema` table and one external statement trigger. The script
creates and drops its own uniquely named PostgreSQL database.

```text
{
  "after": {
    "hash": "46488bed6cae2d389ac7a82ca7c8ffe31c214d36f83be406091862c76d5bfdb2",
    "triggerCount": 1
  },
  "before": {
    "hash": "42bc441236a7512dd41b9b78d738d9de835bf5201578a17f918f25db1d9794e5",
    "triggerCount": 0
  },
  "migrationNeeded": true
}
```

### Expected behavior

Migration-owned triggers that are absent from target entity metadata should
remain in the live database but should not be copied into the entity-metadata
snapshot. ORM-managed triggers declared through `EntitySchema.triggers` must
continue to round-trip normally.

### Additional context

The behavior comes from `Migrator.runMigrations()`: after `up`/`down`, it
introspects the live schema and compares/stores it without distinguishing
metadata-managed triggers from migration-owned external triggers.

A local proof-of-concept filters introspected triggers against
`schemaGenerator.getTargetSchema()` before snapshot comparison/storage. It
keeps the external-trigger snapshot byte-identical with
`checkSchema() === false`, while a separate `EntitySchema.triggers` control also
stays byte-identical and retains its managed trigger.

Versions used:

- MikroORM 7.1.8
- PostgreSQL 17.9
- Node.js 24.14.1
- pnpm 11.13.0

Finds limited to indexes
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

It's very common of many teams - the one I'm part of at work included - to forget about database indexes, until they've already observed slow queries on production. I believe this is in no small part due to the relative "transparency" of indexes at the application level (at least, that's my excuse when I accidentally do it... not knowing there wasn't an index on that column, combined with being in a hurry, and staging appearing to work fine...).

MikroORM entities already contain information about indexes, so the ORM could potentially take the next step in guiding the developer to use these indexes.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

`find*()` methods should include some way to set the filtering and ordering indexes used by the `find*()` method per entity type, which should in turn limit the filtering and ordering to only be of properties participating in the listed indexes. To further ensure no full table scans occur, it should require that there's no gap in the columns used (i.e. if the index is for columns "A, B, C", you can't call with a filter/order on "B" without adding a filter/order for "A" as well, but you don't have to include "C"). Ideally, indexes with expressions should also be supported and somehow expressible.

There should ideally also by `findOneByIndex()`, where it would only allow the full use of a given unique index for filtering the root entity, while still allowing non-unique indexes on the populated fields' indexes, for cases like finding a user by email, while reminding the developer to add an index on the email column.

If extending the current `find*()` method seems like giving them too many responsibilities and/or making those calls too error prone, dedicated methods (`indexedFind*()`?) would also do the job. In fact, a dedicated method may try to infer the indexes used, and error on TS level if a query would result in some part of the select not using an index, be it at the root query or a subquery, be it at the where or odder by level. I'm personally ok with having to specify the index names, especially if they're part of an auto-complete, but I recognize that's an extra burden for many devs.

At runtime, this option/method may also include adding index hints (`USE INDEX`) to further guide the DB into using those indexes where it might otherwise not, though the more important part IMO is team agreement to always include that option (or use of that method, if a separate method), combined with the type safety it gives. That is, this prevents accidentally causing a full table scan after a refactor, where an index was previously used, and makes it easier to review when diagnosing performance issues ("Oh, we're not using the indexes option here? Most likely we're missing some index... let's try to use it... hm, yes, this one column is not part of any index... let's add it...").

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Custom repositories with such find methods could be made during entity generation, but without some first class EntityManager support, the generated ones would be limited to the root entity of a query, without this same feature applied to any of its populated fields.

Searches by unique index via such a generated method  (e.g. `findOneByEmail()` for finding a user by email) would probably be very useful even in that form, but beyond those (e.g. getting a given user's unpaid invoices, where it turns out you're missing an index over the invoice's statuses...) would be impossible to express.

items.body:
### Describe the bug

So, I'm trying to have a m:n relation from a class to the same class, as in:

```
export const ContentSchema = new EntitySchema<BaseContent>({
    name: 'Content',
    abstract: true,
    tableName: 'contents',
    discriminatorColumn: 'type',
    properties: {
        pid: { type: 'string', primary: true },
        catalogName: { type: 'string', primary: true },
```

items.title: Typesafety of `where: {…}` builder struggles with unions
Allow using `setClass` on an `EntitySchema` to enable custom functionality avoiding boilerplate
items.body:
Currently to add extra functionality to entities without using decorators requires setting up a full class object with all the properties and then duplicating that boilerplate with `defineEntity`. It would be nice to instead be able to extend the internal class that `defineEntity` creates and add extra functions etc…

Here's a full example of what we'd like to see:

SQL Table:

```
create table users (
  _id uuid primary key,
  _seq int8 not null,
  _extra jsonb not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null,
  updated_at timestamptz not null,
  first_name text not null,
  last_name text not null,
  email text not null,
  pager_number text,
  phone_number text,
  status_type text not null,
  status_at timestamptz,
  position_role_category text,
  position_role text,
  position_name text
)
```

Example:

```
import { defineEntity} from "@mikro-orm/core"
import { MikroORM } from "@mikro-orm/postgresql"

const UserStatusSchema = defineEntity({
  name: "UserStatus",
  abstract: true,
  embeddable: true,
  discriminatorColumn: "type",
  properties: (p) => ({
    type: p.enum(["available", "unavailable", "unknown"]).name("type"),
  }),
})

const UserStatusAvailableSchema = defineEntity({
  name: "UserStatusAvailable",
  extends: UserStatusSchema,
  discriminatorValue: "available",
  embeddable: true,
  properties: (p) => ({
    at: p.datetime().name("at"),
  }),
})

const UserStatusUnavailableSchema = defineEntity({
  name: "UserStatusUnavailable",
  extends: UserStatusSchema,
  discriminatorValue: "unavailable",
  embeddable: true,
  properties: (p) => ({
    at: p.datetime().name("at"),
  }),
})

const UserStatusUnknownSchema = defineEntity({
  name: "UserStatusUnknown",
  extends: UserStatusSchema,
  discriminatorValue: "unknown",
  embeddable: true,
  properties: (p) => ({
    at: p.datetime().name("at").nullable(),
  }),
})

const UserPositionSchema = defineEntity({
  name: "UserPosition",
  embeddable: true,
  properties: (p) => ({
    discipline: p.string().name("role_category"),
    role: p.string().name("role"),
    name: p.string().name("name"),
  }),
})

const UserSchema = defineEntity({
  tableName: "users",
  name: "User",
  properties: (p) => ({
    id: p.uuid().primary().name("_id"),
    sequence: p.bigint().unique().name("_seq"),
    extra: p.json().name("_extra").default("{}").hidden(),
    createdAt: p.datetime().name("created_at"),
    updatedAt: p.datetime().name("updated_at"),
    firstName: p.string().name("first_name"),
    lastName: p.string().name("last_name"),
    email: p.string().name("email").default(""),
    phoneNumber: p.string().name("phone_number").nullable(),
    pagerNumber: p.string().name("pager_number").nullable(),
    status: p.embedded(UserStatusSchema),
    position: p.embedded(UserPositionSchema).nullable(),
  }),
})

const orm = await MikroORM.init({
  entities: [
    UserStatusAvailableSchema,
    UserStatusUnavailableSchema,
    UserStatusUnknownSchema,
    UserStatusSchema,
    UserPositionSchema,
    UserSchema,
  ],
  dbName: "mikro",
  user: "postgres",
  password: "",
  host: "localhost",
  port: 5432,
})
```

It would be ideal if one could do something like this to add extra functionality to the built-in class and have mikro-orm use that new class:

```
class User extends UserSchema.class {
  fullName() {
    return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`
  }
}

UserSchema.setClass(User)
```

Currently this code throws an error saying duplicate table names are not allowed.
